Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from my side and a couple asks so we can draft a short pricing+pilot proposal: 

Recap of today's discovery:
- Goal: add an in-app assistant to surface care plan guidance and triage questions to reduce care team load and speed patient responses.
- Primary users: care coordinators + patients (triggered messages, 1:1 flows, and a triage shortcut).
- Success metrics discussed: 20% reduction in coordinator time on triage, 2% lift in completed follow-ups.

As discussed, we need three datapoints to model unit economics for the feature and check CAC payback:
1) Expected token volume (rough) — average tokens per interaction and expected monthly token volume for months 1 / 6 / 12.
2) Target monthly budget range for inference (what you are comfortable committing to in an initial pilot).
3) Product pricing targets / acceptable payback horizon (months to CAC payback, margin targets).

I attached a short workbook (redwood_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx) with a spot for the numbers — if you can drop the high-level numbers there it will help. As a starting point, if you have an initial monthly inference budget range (even a band like $10k–$30k) we can run feature-level $/feature and payback scenarios.

Proposed next steps:
- Sarah: share approx tokens/month and budget range (reply to this thread or drop in the workbook).
- Redwood (Vivek/Ben/Priyom): we’ll produce 2 scenarios (conservative / aggressive) showing $/1M tokens required to meet a target 30% gross margin at your price points and CAC payback assumptions.

If it helps I can also schedule a quick 30-min workback session with your product ops team to walk the workbook.

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Recap + ask: token volumes, budget range, and margin targets

Marissa — copying the quick analysis I ran after today's call. I used the assumptions Sarah gave verbally on the call plus a conservative per-interaction token estimate (full prompt+response = 1,200 tokens). See the attached CSV for line-by-line math.

High-level assumptions I used:
- Interaction tokens (avg): 1,200 tokens per end-user interaction (includes system prompt + response).
- Initial MAU generating interactions: 2,000 active users -> ~4,000 interactions/mo = ~4.8M tokens/mo (month-1).
- Growth: 10% MoM; month-12 ~ 20M tokens/mo.
- Target gross margin on inference: 30% (Redwood net price to customer less our incremental cost).
- Customer target price per feature: we left as TBD — I modeled three price points: $20/user/mo (paywalled feature), $5/user/mo (opt-in benefit), and purely cost-only (no direct charge).

Quick results (rounded):
- To hit 30% margin at customer price $5/user/mo with 2,000 users and 4.8M tokens/mo, Redwood would need to offer ~$250 / 1M tokens (customer-facing price) to meet the target margin. At $20/user/mo the required $/1M tokens is much higher (~$1,000 /1M tokens) because the revenue per feature is larger.
- If customer has a monthly inference budget band of $10k–$25k, that maps to ~40M–100M tokens per month at a $250 /1M token list price; conversely, at $1,000 /1M tokens that budget only covers 10M–25M tokens.

CAC payback (very rough):
- Assume CAC per closed account for this feature is $45k (includes CS ramp + pilot support + discounting).
- With a $5/user/mo price and 2k users paying, revenue = $10k/mo. Payback = 4.5 months (base churn ignored).
- When modeling embedding inference as an add-on cost, incremental gross margin on the feature (after inference cost) needs to be evaluated to ensure payback remains <9 months.

Actionable asks for the model to be useful:
1) Confirm whether the feature will be charged to customers (and at which tier).
2) Confirm expected MAU that will use the assistant during pilot (2k used above is my conservative read).
3) Tell us if you expect many long context interactions (>2k tokens) — that changes per-interaction token estimate.

Attaching: feature-econ-scenarios.csv (models for price points and token bands). I can turn this into a slidedeck if we need to present to their procurement.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: feature-econ-scenarios.csv (csv, 45KB)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and to Ben for the quick math. A few clarifications from our side to populate the workbook: 

Our numbers (high-level):
- Pilot cohort: 2,500 patients (care coordinators = ~25 users). We expect ~1.6 interactions per patient per month initially.
- Average tokens per interaction: we expect ~900 tokens (most are short prompts + template responses, but occasionally longer).
- Estimated month-1 tokens: 2,500 * 1.6 * 900 = ~3.6M tokens. Month-6 target: ~9M tokens. Month-12: ~18–22M tokens (depending on adoption).
- Pilot monthly inference budget: $12k–$20k (we could flex if value is proven).
- Pricing/monetization: likely bundled into premium tier; internal leadership wants payback <= 9 months and net margin on the feature >= 25% after inference cost.

Additional asks: can you show (in the scenarios) an example where we keep customer charge at $8/user/mo but you (Redwood) provide a trial discount in month-1 to shorten payback? Also can we get a line item showing expected latency/throughput impact at 20M tokens/mo (we have SLA concerns).

Happy to jump on a 30-min session tomorrow to walk through the workbook.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Product, LumaHealth
